subject: Nebula Apps integration launch: SDK, migration, and rate-safety plan
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@nebulaapps.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Nebula Apps DevOps <devops@nebulaapps.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nebula Apps – Integration kickoff & runtime questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nebula's product team is excited to move to a short pilot. Before we lock dates, two quick asks so we can scope the implementation sprint: 

1) SDK / sample code: we want an end-to-end SDK example (node/python) that shows the auth flow, streaming, and an example of a batch-embedding call.
2) Endpoint migration plan: our current inference calls hit a self-hosted endpoint. We need guidance on switching traffic to Redwood (canary strategy, DNS cutover, session continuity).
3) Retries/timeouts & rate limits: recommended client-side timeout and retry/backoff settings for low-latency user flows and a high-throughput batch job overnight.

We target a sandbox cutover the week of Sep 20. Can your team put forward a short runbook and a list of artifacts we should prepare from our side?

Thanks — looping in Onn (DevOps) for infra details.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, Nebula Apps
cell: +1-415-555-0198

Hi Samira — great to hear you're ready to pilot. Monica and I will own the technical handoff and runbook; Vivek will join for final rollout ops.

Quick answers and next steps:
- We can provide a compact SDK repo (Node + Python) with streaming examples and a batch embedding helper. We'll attach a sample bundle and an implementation checklist.
- For endpoint migration we typically recommend: 1) canary traffic split (5-10%), 2) prefix/KV cache warmup, 3) progressive ramp to 50% during a low-traffic window, 4) DNS cutover or switch the upstream gateway once stable. Full checklist attached.
- Client-side best-practices (summary):
  * User-facing calls: timeout = 6s default, single retry with jittered backoff (250ms initial).
  * Streaming: keep-keepalive 30s; reconnect with incremental backoff.
  * Batch jobs: use long timeouts (60–120s), explicit pagination, and chunk payloads to avoid timeouts.

Can you share: sandbox API keys (or a short-lived JWT), expected qps for user flows, and an example batch job size? If you can get those to us by Sep 14 we’ll produce a tailored runbook by Sep 16.

I’m attaching a mutual action plan template to this thread.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Samira / Onn — Monica here from Implementation. Per Irene's note, attaching a compact artifact set and a tactical checklist. High-level plan below plus the sample snippets.

1) SDK & sample code (attached: nebula-sample-snippets.tar.gz)
  - Node + Python small examples: auth (API key + short-lived JWT), streaming chat, batch-embeddings helper.
  - Directory layout and quick start in README; run locally with REDWOOD_API_KEY env var.

2) Endpoint migration (recommended sequence)
  - Prep (D-7): provide sandbox keys; we advise a mirror path so you post to /v1/redwood/proxy during warmup.
  - Canary (D0): route 5% traffic to Redwood; monitor latency, error-rate, token usage.
  - Ramp (D1–D2): if error-rate < 0.5% and 95th p95 latency within SLA, increase to 25% then 50%.
  - Cutover (D3): DNS TTL drop + gateway config switch; maintain fallback to legacy for 30m.
  - Rollback criteria: sustained errors > 1% for 10m or latency > 2x baseline.

3) Retries/timeouts & rate handling
  - Client defaults we recommend: user-facing sync calls: timeout=6000ms, maxAttempts=2, backoffInitial=250ms, backoffFactor=2.0, jitter=0.2.
  - Streaming: keep-alive pings, client reconnect backoff: 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s; resume with KV cache token when possible to avoid reprocessing.
  - Batch uploads: chunk to <= 2k records per request, timeout=90s, parallelism 4–8 workers; use exponential backoff with full jitter for 429s.
  - Rate limits: track 429/503s centrally; implement token bucket local limiter with 200ms token refill granularity.

4) Observability & fallbacks
  - Add per-call tracing id; send to Redwood via X-Request-ID and our trace hook in SDK.
  - We’ll provide a dashboard for per-route latency and token consumption during the pilot.

Attachments in this thread: nebula-sample-snippets.tar.gz, nebula-migration-checklist.pdf, nebula-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Sample node snippet (from attached bundle):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeout: 6000 });

async function chat() {
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', prompt: 'Hello' });
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
  }
}

If this fits your needs I’ll schedule a 30m technical sync (Monica + Engineer) for Sep 15 to walk through the bundle and validate sandbox access.

—Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — Vivek here, I’ll be the rollout lead on Redwood’s side. A couple tactical notes and contacts below.

Action items I’ll own:
- Validate sandbox performance with Nebula DevOps on Sep 18 (I’ll ping Onn to get keys).
- Stand up a short smoke test harness (we’ll share a Jenkins/GHA job template in the drive).
- Coordinate cutover window (recommended: Sep 22 02:00–04:00 UTC) and monitor with 5m alerting windows.

Operational suggestions:
- During canary we’ll keep automatic fallback enabled so any 5xx/429 spike flips traffic back to your endpoint for 15m while we triage.
- For token usage: enable per-route caps in the first 48h to avoid burst overruns; we suggest a soft cap at 120 rps for the first day and scaling rules after the smoke tests.

Drive links and support: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-integration
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NW-2026-104

Samira/Onn — I’ll send a calendar invite for Sep 15 (technical walkthrough) and Sep 18 (sandbox perf test). If you want to accelerate the timeline, share the sandbox keys and a small sample batch (CSV) and we’ll run against it earlier.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
